entities.summary:
Shabbethai Donnolo was a Graeco-Italian Jewish physician and writer on medicine and astrology, born in 9th-century Sicily, and died in 1006 in Constantinople. As a renowned scholar of the Abbasid Caliphate, Donnolo composed several medical and astrological texts, including the influential 'Kitab al-tibb al-nasawi' (The Book of Nasawi Medicine), which synthesized Greek, Persian, and Arab medical knowledge. His works had a profound impact on the development of medicine in the Mediterranean world, particularly in the Byzantine Empire and the Islamic world. Donnolo's writings also demonstrate his expertise in astrology, which he applied to the study of celestial bodies and their influence on human affairs. His significance extends beyond his contributions to medicine and astrology, as he represents the cultural exchange and transmission of knowledge between the Byzantine and Abbasid civilizations. 

Shabbethai Donnolo's legacy can be seen in the many scholars who built upon his works, including the famous Jewish physician and scholar, Ibn Sina (Avicenna), who credited Donnolo as an influence. Donnolo's writings also reflect the cosmopolitan nature of the Abbasid Caliphate, which attracted scholars from diverse backgrounds to its court. 

The discovery of Donnolo's works in the 19th century led to a renewed interest in the history of medicine and astrology, and his influence can be seen in the development of modern medical and astrological practices. 

In conclusion, Shabbethai Donnolo's contributions to medicine and astrology have left a lasting impact on the development of these fields, and his significance extends beyond his own works to represent the cultural exchange and transmission of knowledge between the Byzantine and Abbasid civilizations.
